text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Switch EXCAVA to Anthropic’s latest Claude 3.7 Sonnet. It’s the only model that consistently outperforms others on complex reasoning tasks, which directly raises EXCAVA’s capability ceiling. The trade-off is higher cost per token, but the 0.5%+ gain in precision justifies it.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t just cost—it’s benchmark drift. EXCAVA’s live task accuracy already lags Sonnet 3.7’s promised 0.7% gain by 0.3% in our last run; switching models mid-stream could widen that gap if the new model’s strengths don’t align with our specific prompt chains. Test Sonnet 3.7 on a 500-sample slice of our production data first—if the delta holds, switch; if not, fall back to the current model and audit why the gap exists.

name: Gearbox
text:
Switch EXCAVA to Anthropic’s latest Claude 3.7 Sonnet for the 500-sample test run. Its 0.7% benchmark gain over our current model is the highest confirmed uplift available, and the 0.3% gap Torque flagged is smaller than the risk of staying put. The trade-off is the test’s upfront cost, but that’s a one-time burn to avoid locking in a 0.3% deficit. If the test hits the 0.5%+ mark, we roll it out; if not, we pivot immediately.

name: Torque
text: The real risk is benchmark drift plus prompt misalignment: Sonnet 3.7’s 0.7% gain is measured on static benchmarks, not our live prompt chains where it already trails by 0.3%. Run a 500-sample A/B test with a frozen prompt set and a strict accuracy metric—if Sonnet 3.7 gains <0.4% on live data, it’s not worth the cost; if it gains >0.5%, switch immediately.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 500-sample blind A/B test on EXCAVA comparing current model vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet with frozen prompts and strict accuracy metric; if gain ≥0.4%, switch permanently. Owned by Torque.
